description: OPT-IN merge-queue mode: batch several finished tasklist branches, verify the batch TIP ONCE, and binary-bisect on failure to isolate the culprit — merging only the branches that pass. Today chief pays the full verification cost N times for N tasklists (serialized rebase -> re-verify -> --no-ff, one at a time). At the ~360-tasklist scale this portfolio is heading to, that is the dominant cost of the merge phase. Prior art: GASTOWN (github.com/steveyegge/gastown, 17,551 stars, MIT, active) ships a Bors-style merge queue whose 'Refinery' batches pending merge requests, rebases them as a stack on main, runs the verification gates on the batch tip once, and on failure binary-bisects the stack to find the offending branch — amortizing verification across N merges instead of paying it N times. Bors has run this design for 10+ years. THE HARD CONSTRAINT, and the reason this is a MODE and not a replacement: the serialized rebase -> re-verify -> --no-ff floor STAYS THE DEFAULT and remains chief's correctness guarantee (docs/explanation/drivers-and-safety.md). Batching is opted into per run; with the flag absent, behaviour is byte-for-byte what it is today. The second hard constraint is DETERMINISM: bisect is only sound when verification is a deterministic function of the tree, and band 88's quality ratchet adds a new axis whose signal is a METRIC DELTA measured on a batch tip — which is NOT trivially attributable to a single branch (two branches can each be individually within tolerance while their combination regresses, and a ratchet is path-dependent in a way a test suite is not). US-3 exists solely to settle that: either the regression is attributed correctly, or the batch is rejected wholesale and the queue falls back to the serialized floor — never a guess. It also interacts with band 91: a branch touching a `review`-policy overlap zone must not be smuggled into main inside a batch. Scope: `engine/driver.sh` (merge phase + scheduler), `engine/lib.sh` (verify_branch), `.chief/config` + `templates/`, `bin/chief`, `docs/explanation/drivers-and-safety.md` + `docs/reference/verify-hook.md`, `test/`. NOTE ON WHAT IS BEING ADOPTED: this is one mechanism, not the project — Gastown's own docs state it lacks dependency resolution across tasks and acceptance-criteria ledgers, which are exactly chief's differentiators (`dependsOn`/`touches` scheduling, the per-story `passes` ledger, the cross-repo run registry). Take the Refinery's batching + bisect; keep everything else. See rosetta/strategy/DECISIONS.md D1 and F7.

userStories.title: Batch formation behind an explicit opt-in, with the serialized floor untouched as the default
userStories.description: Add a merge-queue mode that collects several merge-ready branches, stacks them on the base, and verifies the batch tip once. It must be impossible to enter this mode by accident.
acceptanceCriteria: A merge-queue mode is opt-in PER RUN and per repo — a `chief run` flag (e.g. `--merge-batch[=N]`) and/or a `.chief/config` setting, both documented and both DEFAULTING OFF; with the option absent, the merge phase executes the existing serialized rebase -> re-verify -> `--no-ff` path with no behavioural difference whatsoever (a test asserts the default path is unchanged)

When enabled, the merge phase collects up to N merge-ready branches into a batch, rebases each onto the running batch tip IN A DETERMINISTIC ORDER (documented — e.g. completion order, ties broken by tasklist name, so a batch is reproducible), and runs the verify gate ONCE on the resulting tip rather than once per branch

A batch is only ever formed from branches that are ALREADY merge-ready under today's rules: the agent loop reached COMPLETE, the no-work guard passed, and the branch rebases cleanly onto the tip. A branch that hits a rebase conflict is EJECTED from the batch (labelled exactly as today) and the batch re-forms without it — one bad rebase never fails the whole batch
Batch size is bounded and configurable with a documented default, and a batch of one is exactly the serialized path (no special case, no divergent code)

Merges still happen with `--no-ff`, one commit per tasklist, and merge ordering is still SERIALIZED against the base — the batch is a verification-amortization device, never concurrent writes to `main`
Bash 3.2 compatible; `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S error` clean

userStories.title: Binary-bisect a failing batch and merge only the branches that pass
userStories.description: On a red batch tip, isolate the culprit by bisection rather than discarding the whole batch — the payoff that makes batching worth doing.
acceptanceCriteria: A failing batch tip triggers a BINARY BISECT over the stacked branches: verify the tip of the first half, recurse into the failing half, and continue until the offending branch is isolated — worst case O(log N) extra verifications, and the number of verifications performed is recorded in the run log so the amortization is measurable rather than asserted

The isolated culprit is left in exactly the state a serialized failure leaves it in TODAY — labelled `VERIFY-FAILED`, branch and worktree kept, eligible for the existing bounded re-arm/retry — and the remaining branches in the batch are merged (re-forming a batch from the survivors is permitted; merging them one by one is also acceptable, but which happens is documented)

MULTIPLE culprits in one batch terminate: after isolating and ejecting one failing branch, the surviving stack is re-verified and re-bisected as needed, with a documented bound on total attempts so a pathological batch degrades to the serialized floor rather than looping

Bisect is DEFENDED AGAINST NON-DETERMINISM: the docs state plainly that bisect assumes the verify gate is a deterministic function of the tree, and a flaky gate is detected rather than trusted — a bisect whose result is inconsistent with a confirming re-verification of the isolated branch ABANDONS the bisect and falls back to serialized re-verification of every branch in the batch (correct, just slower). A wrong branch is never blamed on the strength of one observation
Every path through batching and bisecting ends with the same invariant the serialized floor guarantees: nothing reaches `$CHIEF_BASE_BRANCH` that has not had a green verify on a tree containing it
Bash 3.2 compatible; `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S error` clean

userStories.title: Settle ratchet attribution and overlap-zone policy inside a batch
userStories.description: Band 88 adds a non-boolean, path-dependent gate axis and band 91 adds a human-approval gate; both change what a batch tip's result means. State the semantics and enforce them — do not let batching silently weaken either.
acceptanceCriteria: The tasklist's chosen policy for a QUALITY-RATCHET regression measured on a batch tip is stated explicitly in `docs/` and implemented: a ratchet delta on a batch tip is NOT trivially attributable to one branch (two branches each within tolerance can jointly regress a metric, and duplication/decomposition metrics are inherently cross-branch), so the gate must either (a) attribute the regression mechanically — by re-measuring 88's metric record per-branch against the base over that branch's own changed-file scope, and blaming a branch only when its individual delta exceeds the tolerance — or (b) REJECT THE BATCH WHOLESALE and fall back to serialized rebase -> re-verify for its members. A metric delta is never guessed at, and a regression is never allowed through because no single branch could be blamed

A ratchet regression that is attributable to no single branch (each member individually green, the combination red) is a first-class, NAMED outcome: it is reported as such, the batch is dissolved, and the members are re-run through the serialized floor — where, if the regression is real and joint, the second branch to merge is correctly blocked by the ratchet against the already-merged first

Band 91's overlap zones survive batching: a branch touching a `review`-policy zone is NEVER merged as a batch member on the strength of a batch-tip verify — it either waits for its explicit approval before it is eligible for a batch at all, or is excluded from batching entirely (whichever is chosen is documented, and the choice is enforced by a test)
The diff-size budget from 91 is evaluated per BRANCH, not per batch tip, so a batch cannot dilute an oversized diff into an aggregate that clears the budget

`docs/explanation/drivers-and-safety.md` gains a merge-queue section that PRESERVES the existing honest framing — the serialized floor is the correctness guarantee, batching is an opt-in throughput optimization layered above it — and states, in one place, the determinism assumption, the ratchet-attribution rule, and the overlap-zone rule
Bash 3.2 compatible; `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S error` clean

userStories.title: Pin the whole mechanism with a hermetic test
userStories.description: Prove the three behaviours that make batching safe, using the existing scripted-fake-agent harness — offline, temp prefixes, no real ~/.chief.
acceptanceCriteria: A hermetic test (in `test/`, using the existing scripted fake `claude` on `PATH` + temp prefixes, offline) asserts: a CLEAN batch of N branches merges all N with exactly ONE verification of the batch tip

The same test asserts: a batch containing exactly one bad branch BISECTS, isolates that branch, merges only the good ones, and leaves the bad one `VERIFY-FAILED` with its branch and worktree intact — and that the total verification count matches the O(log N) bound rather than N

The same test asserts the ratchet case: a batch in which a tracked quality metric regresses is either attributed to the correct single branch (that branch blocked, the rest merged) or rejected wholesale with the named not-attributable outcome and its members re-run serialized — and that in NEITHER case does a regressing tree reach the base branch
The test asserts the negative control that matters most: with the opt-in flag absent, the merge phase is the serialized floor and performs exactly N verifications for N tasklists
